tickets.title: RC Web Dev tracker
tickets.description: RC Web Dev board at #/rc-web-dev. Rainbow profile item. Rainbow user ring only while on this page. Drag columns, ticket sheet, create, priorities.
acceptanceCriteria: The tracker is available at #/rc-web-dev.
Tickets can be viewed, created, opened, prioritized, and moved through the workflow.

tickets.title: QA: drag tickets between columns
tickets.description: Drag a ticket to another column. A shadow follows the cursor and a placeholder shows the drop. The card stays in the new column after refresh.
acceptanceCriteria: Dragging a ticket shows a visible card shadow and drop placeholder.
After a valid drop and page refresh, the ticket remains in the destination column.

tickets.title: QA: ticket sheet
tickets.description: Click a ticket. Sheet opens with status, priority, description, and related links. Close with X, backdrop, or Escape. Related rows open that ticket.
acceptanceCriteria: Selecting a ticket opens a sheet showing its current status, priority, description, and related tickets.
The sheet closes with the X button, backdrop click, or Escape key, and related-ticket rows open the selected ticket.

tickets.title: QA: create ticket
tickets.description: Use Create ticket or + on Ideas. Title, priority, assigned (CZ or KC), category, description. New tickets get an RC-xx id.
acceptanceCriteria: Create Ticket and the Ideas-column add button open a form with title, priority, assignee, category, and description fields.
Submitting valid data creates one ticket with the next available RC-xx ID and displays it in Ideas.

tickets.title: QA: roadmap groups
tickets.description: Roadmap is grouped by category and collapsed when a group is already done. Unassigned Ideas sit below, grouped by category, and do not count in the percentage.
acceptanceCriteria: The roadmap groups tickets under the correct category and collapses categories whose tickets are all complete.
Unassigned Ideas appear below the roadmap and are excluded from completion-percentage calculations.

tickets.title: Logs, pills, groups stay put
tickets.description: Logs tab. New / Updated / In progress pills as the stand-in for later approval. A move keeps the ticket’s category. The destination group opens and gets a bouncing dot on the category title — no blue ring around the section.
acceptanceCriteria: Creating, editing, and moving tickets produces accurate entries in the Logs tab and the correct review pill.
Moving a ticket preserves its category, opens the destination group, and highlights that category with the intended indicator.

tickets.title: Ideas column: headers stay, tickets scroll
tickets.description: In Ideas, category headers always stay in the column. An open group’s tickets scroll in the space above the headers below it. No nested column-plus-group scroll. Soft Tailwind tints per category — not solid 600 bars.
acceptanceCriteria: Category headers remain visible while tickets in an expanded Ideas group scroll within the available space.
The Ideas column has a single clear scrolling behavior and retains the configured soft category colours.

tickets.title: 1:1 with Kevin — tomorrow
tickets.description: Carlos (CZ) one-on-one with Kevin Collins (KC). Friday 14 Aug 2026. Walk through the board, logs, and what is in progress.
acceptanceCriteria: The board walkthrough covers current progress, logs, priorities, and open decisions.
Decisions and follow-up actions from the meeting are captured in the relevant tickets.

tickets.title: Persist RC Web Dev tickets in Supabase
tickets.description: Holding store until FileMaker. Tables rc_tickets and rc_ticket_logs. Create, move, and edit on the board should save there so work survives refresh. Do not run live Supabase commands without asking first (.cursor/rules/supabase-permission.mdc).
acceptanceCriteria: Creating, editing, or moving a ticket writes the corresponding ticket and log data to Supabase.
Reloading the application restores the latest saved ticket states without duplicating tickets or logs.

tickets.title: Catalogue
tickets.description: Catalogue page. Three products, same price and pack size. Bilingual is the product name, not navbar language.
acceptanceCriteria: The catalogue displays the English, Bilingual, and French business-card products.
Selecting any catalogue product opens the correct details page.

tickets.title: Business Card English
tickets.description: $63 per box, 250 cards.
acceptanceCriteria: The English business card is labelled correctly and displays a price of $63 per box.
The product shows that one box contains 250 printed business cards.

tickets.title: Business Card Bilingual
tickets.description: Product name, not the EN/FR toggle.
acceptanceCriteria: The Bilingual business card appears as a distinct product with the correct product name.
Selecting it does not change the application interface language.

tickets.title: Business Card French
tickets.description: $63 per box, 250 cards.
acceptanceCriteria: The French business card is labelled correctly and displays a price of $63 per box.
The product shows that one box contains 250 printed business cards.

tickets.title: Catalogue price and pack size
tickets.description: $63 per box (shipping included), 250 cards per box, shown on the catalogue.
acceptanceCriteria: Every catalogue card displays $63 per box and 250 cards per box.
Price and pack-size wording is consistent across all three products.
tickets.notes: USER.md. The $63 box fee includes shipping; cart Shipping & Handling stays $0.00.

tickets.title: Card details
tickets.description: Details page: packaging, print on demand, pricing table, materials / brand notes.
acceptanceCriteria: The details page shows packaging, pricing, materials, and brand information for the selected product.
The user can continue from product details to card customization.

tickets.title: Packaging 250/BX
tickets.description: Details page shows packaging 250/BX.
acceptanceCriteria: The details page clearly states that one box contains 250 cards.
The pack-size value is consistent with the catalogue and cart calculations.

tickets.title: Pricing table
tickets.description: Details page pricing tiers.
acceptanceCriteria: The pricing table displays the configured quantity tiers and corresponding prices.
Tier values are readable and do not conflict with the $63-per-box base price.

tickets.title: Materials / brand notes
tickets.description: Details page materials and brand notes.
acceptanceCriteria: The details page displays the approved material specifications.
The Colliers brand notes are visible and associated with the selected card product.

tickets.title: Customize card
tickets.description: Vue customize is ahead of the designer. Do not copy AI Studio customize.
acceptanceCriteria: The customization form supports all approved personal and office fields.
Valid customization data can be previewed and added to the cart without losing the entered values.

tickets.title: Live preview
tickets.description: Preview updates as fields change.
acceptanceCriteria: Changing a supported customization field updates the card preview immediately.
The preview matches the values currently entered or selected in the form.

tickets.title: Full name (max 50, two lines)
tickets.description: Name field max 50 characters, two lines on the card. Vue still caps at 30.
acceptanceCriteria: The full-name field accepts no more than 50 characters.
A valid long name renders on no more than two lines without overlapping other card content.
The field accepts 1–50 characters after leading and trailing spaces are removed; a 51st character cannot be stored or submitted.
A 50-character name remains readable within the approved two-line name area at supported widths; it does not overlap the designation, contact details, logo, or card edge.
An empty or whitespace-only name blocks Add to Cart and shows field-level guidance.

tickets.title: Designation dropdown (one per card)
tickets.description: Vue today: one designation per card from the dropdown. Multiple designations is USR-039.
acceptanceCriteria: The user can select one available designation from the dropdown.
The selected designation appears correctly on the live preview and saved cart item.
tickets.notes: USER.md · BUSINESS-RULES.md section 4 · CU-02 / CU-03 are USR-039

tickets.title: Email (max 40)
tickets.description: Email max 40. Vue still caps at 30. Limit decided in IDEA-01.
acceptanceCriteria: The email field accepts no more than 40 characters.
The accepted email value appears unchanged on the preview and cart item.
The field accepts a syntactically valid email of up to 40 characters after surrounding spaces are removed; 41 characters are rejected.
Invalid formats and whitespace-only values block Add to Cart and show field-level guidance without clearing the entered value.
A 40-character email is displayed gracefully in the preview without overlapping adjacent card content; the stored cart value is not truncated.

tickets.title: Mobile phone Canadian +1
tickets.description: Canadian +1, formatted as the user types.
acceptanceCriteria: The phone field accepts a Canadian number with the +1 country code.
Digits are formatted consistently while typing and the final value appears correctly on the preview.

tickets.title: Office address dropdown
tickets.description: Colliers offices from products.js. Later wire to ADM-067.
acceptanceCriteria: The office dropdown lists only configured Colliers office addresses.
Selecting an office updates the card preview and the selection remains on the cart item.

tickets.title: Company and website locked
tickets.description: Company Colliers. Website colliers.com/canada.
acceptanceCriteria: Company is displayed as Colliers and cannot be edited by the user.
Website is displayed as colliers.com/canada and cannot be edited by the user.

tickets.title: Add to Cart quantity 1
tickets.description: Each Add to Cart click adds quantity 1.
acceptanceCriteria: Each Add to Cart action adds exactly one box for the configured card.
The cart badge and line quantity increase by one without losing customization details.

tickets.title: Allow users to select multiple designations
tickets.description: One or more designations from the available list. Selected values appear below the field and on the preview. A selected designation can be removed. Vue still allows one.
acceptanceCriteria: Users can select more than one designation.
Selected designations appear below the field, on the card preview, and the control shows how many are selected.
Users can remove a selected designation.
Removed designations disappear from the preview.
The same designation cannot be selected more than once, and the selected-value count equals the number of unique selections.
Selection order is preserved in the preview and in the cart item so equality checks are deterministic.
If the approved maximum number of designations is reached, additional choices are disabled or rejected with clear guidance.
tickets.notes: USER.md · F-24 · BUSINESS-RULES.md CU-02, CU-03. Current Vue is one designation (USR-033).

tickets.title: Cart
tickets.description: Cart drawer: add, quantity, combine same details, keep different name or title separate.
acceptanceCriteria: The cart displays every added card with its customization, box quantity, and price.
Users can update quantities or clear the cart and totals recalculate correctly.

tickets.title: Combine same product and details
tickets.description: Same product + same details combine into one cart item.
acceptanceCriteria: Cards with the same product and identical customization are combined into one cart line.
Combining lines increases quantity without changing the saved customization data.
Equality includes product, normalized full name, ordered designation IDs, normalized email, normalized phone, and office-address ID; changing any one value creates a separate cart line.
Adding an identical configuration repeatedly increments only its box quantity and never replaces the original configuration or shipping assignment.

tickets.title: Separate cart items for different name or title
tickets.description: Different name or title stay separate rows. TC-05 / TC-05b.
acceptanceCriteria: Cards with different names remain separate cart lines.
Cards with different titles or designation selections remain separate cart lines.

tickets.title: Cart badge icon
tickets.description: Red number on the header cart icon = total quantity.
acceptanceCriteria: The header badge equals the total number of boxes across all cart lines.
The badge updates immediately after adding, removing, clearing, or changing quantity.

tickets.title: Clear cart
tickets.description: Empty the cart. Badge goes to 0.
acceptanceCriteria: Clear Cart removes every cart line after the action is confirmed.
The cart badge and cart totals return to zero.

tickets.title: Change quantity in cart / shipping
tickets.description: Qty on a cart line. Shipping location qty does not change cart qty.
acceptanceCriteria: Changing a cart-line quantity updates its subtotal and the order total.
Changing a shipping-location allocation does not modify the cart-line quantity.
Cart quantity accepts whole numbers only, has a minimum of 1 box, and rejects blank, zero, negative, decimal, or non-numeric values.
After a valid quantity change, printed-card count equals quantity × 250 and line total equals quantity × $63.00.
A quantity change cannot leave shipping-location allocations above or below the ordered box quantity without a visible validation state.

tickets.title: Show printed-card count (qty × 250)
tickets.description: Quantity 3 = 750 printed cards = $189.00. Vue shows boxes and price only.
acceptanceCriteria: Each cart and review line displays printed-card total as box quantity multiplied by 250.
For quantity 3, the interface shows 750 printed cards and a $189 line total.
Printed-card counts use whole numbers with thousands separators and are recalculated immediately after every valid box-quantity change.
The printed-card count is informational and cannot be edited independently of box quantity.

tickets.title: Shipping
tickets.description: Shipping page. $0.00 (included in the $63 box fee). No payment. Location qty does not change cart qty.
acceptanceCriteria: The shipping page displays cart items, shipping groups, and selected locations accurately.
Shipping remains $0.00 and the user can continue without entering payment information.
tickets.notes: USER.md · ShippingPage.vue · F-10. Shipping is not calculated separately — it is built into the $63 card box fee.

tickets.title: Add / remove / select ship-to location
tickets.description: Add, remove, or pick a saved location.
acceptanceCriteria: The user can add or select a saved ship-to location for a shipping group.
The user can remove an assigned location without deleting or changing the cart item.
Only saved, active addresses are selectable; selecting the same address twice in one group does not create a duplicate location row.
Removing a location that has an allocation requires confirmation or returns its allocation to an unassigned state that blocks submission.

tickets.title: Location qty vs cart qty
tickets.description: Qty on a location does not change cart quantity.
acceptanceCriteria: A location allocation can be changed independently within its shipping group.
Changing the allocation does not change the original cart quantity or order total.
Location quantities accept whole boxes only and cannot be negative, decimal, or greater than the remaining unallocated quantity for the product.
For each product, the sum of location quantities across all shipping groups must equal its cart quantity before Review or Submit is enabled.
Changing an allocation updates the remaining-unallocated value immediately but never changes price, cart badge, or ordered box quantity.

tickets.title: Shipping $0, no payment
tickets.description: Shipping is $0.00 because it is built into the $63 card box fee. There is no payment step.
acceptanceCriteria: Shipping cost displays as $0.00 throughout shipping and review.
No credit-card, billing, or payment step is presented before confirmation.
tickets.notes: USER.md. Do not add a shipping-cost calculation. The $63 box fee already includes shipping.

tickets.title: Split Order
tickets.description: Split Order adds a shipping group. Empty-group behaviour is USR-057. Cannot remove the last split.
acceptanceCriteria: Split Order creates one additional shipping group.
Repeated use creates distinct groups without changing the total ordered quantity.
Shipping groups receive stable sequential labels and unique internal keys so repeated split/remove actions do not merge group state.
Creating a group does not copy products, locations, allocations, or totals from another group.
tickets.notes: USER.md · F-09 · BUSINESS-RULES.md SH-02. Empty new group is USR-057.

tickets.title: Cannot remove the last split
tickets.description: Remove Split only when there is more than one split.
acceptanceCriteria: Remove Split is available when more than one shipping group exists.
The final remaining shipping group cannot be removed.
Removing a non-final group requires confirmation when it contains a product, address, or allocation.
After removal, no product quantity is lost: affected products return to Shipping Group 1 or become visibly unassigned according to the approved rule.

tickets.title: Move cards between shipping groups
tickets.description: Move a card from group 1 to group 2 without duplicating quantity. Vue still shares one cart across splits.
acceptanceCriteria: A card can be moved from one shipping group to another.
After the move, the card exists only in the destination group and total ordered quantity is unchanged.
The move control lists every other active shipping group and does not list the current group as a destination.
Moving the last product out of a group leaves the group valid and empty; it does not automatically delete the group.
Moving a product preserves its customization and ordered quantity, and clears or revalidates any location allocation that is not valid in the destination group.

tickets.title: Split Order creates an empty group
tickets.description: Split Order creates a new empty shipping group. New cards stay in Shipping Group 1. Vue duplicates the cart view.
acceptanceCriteria: Split Order creates a new group with no cards and no selected address. Products and locations from the existing group are not duplicated.
Existing and newly added cards remain in Shipping Group 1 until the user moves them.
The new group receives the next group number and a unique key even after another group has been removed.
Adding a card after multiple groups exist still assigns it to Shipping Group 1 exactly once.

tickets.title: Colliers offices on shipping, not NJ samples
tickets.description: savedAddresses still seeds South Plainfield / Millville NJ. Customize already uses Colliers offices. See ADM-067.
acceptanceCriteria: Shipping locations contain approved Colliers offices and no New Jersey sample addresses.
The shipping address records use the same fields and values as the managed Colliers office list.
When no approved office is available, the selector shows an empty state and prevents the user from continuing; sample data is not substituted.
Address identity uses the managed address record ID, not a formatted display string, so edits do not create accidental duplicates.

tickets.title: Order confirmed
tickets.description: Success screen. Clears cart and order draft. No payment. User order history is USR-090 (Ideas; still to discuss).
acceptanceCriteria: Submitting a valid reviewed order opens the confirmation screen once.
Successful confirmation clears the cart and shipping draft without creating a payment step. Order History is USR-090.
Submit is disabled while the request is in progress, preventing double-clicks from creating duplicate orders.
A failed submission keeps the cart and shipping draft intact, shows a retryable error, and does not open confirmation.

tickets.title: Success screen
tickets.description: Thank-you / confirmed page after Review / Checkout.
acceptanceCriteria: The confirmation screen clearly states that the order was submitted successfully.
Refreshing or navigating after confirmation does not resubmit the same order.
The confirmation shows a single order reference returned by the submission adapter; it does not generate a second order on refresh.
Direct navigation to confirmation without a successful submission redirects to a safe page or shows a non-success state.

tickets.title: Clear cart and order draft
tickets.description: Confirming clears cart and the shipping draft.
acceptanceCriteria: After confirmation, the cart contains no items and its badge is zero.
Returning to shipping starts with a new empty order draft.
Cart and shipping state are cleared only after the submission adapter returns success; validation or network errors preserve both.
Starting a new order after confirmation creates Shipping Group 1 once and contains no products, locations, or allocations from the prior order.

tickets.title: Order review before confirm
tickets.description: Review products, quantities, shipping groups, and addresses before submit. Vue Review / Checkout goes straight to confirmed. No review route.
acceptanceCriteria: A review step shows every card, box quantity, printed-card total, shipping group, and selected address.
The user can return to correct the order or confirm it without entering payment details.
Review is reachable only when every cart item has a valid configuration and every product is fully allocated to saved shipping locations.
Review totals reconcile: boxes × 250 equals printed cards, boxes × $63.00 equals product total, and shipping displays $0.00.
Back navigation returns to shipping with every group, address, and allocation preserved.

tickets.title: Header language
tickets.description: Navbar EN/FR switches site chrome. Footer language is a duplicate (F-20).
acceptanceCriteria: The header provides the single EN/FR language control for the application.
Changing the language updates supported interface labels without changing the selected product.

tickets.title: Navbar EN/FR
tickets.description: Header EN/FR. Example: Add to Cart → Ajouter au panier.
acceptanceCriteria: Selecting EN displays supported navigation and action labels in English.
Selecting FR displays the corresponding French labels, including Ajouter au panier.
The selected interface language persists while navigating between portal pages during the current session.
Changing EN/FR does not reset form input, cart contents, shipping groups, addresses, quantities, or the selected card product.
Missing translations fall back to the approved default language and expose no raw translation keys to users.

tickets.title: Address Book
tickets.description: The user keeps personal ship-to addresses and can view Colliers offices. Designer: profile → Address Book. Not admin Manage Addresses (ADM-060). Not in Vue. Still to discuss.
acceptanceCriteria: A signed-in user can open Address Book from the profile menu and see personal addresses and Colliers offices.
This page is not admin Manage Addresses (ADM-060). Company office add, edit, and delete stay admin work.
Personal addresses and company offices are visually and functionally separated; regular users cannot mutate company-office records.
Loading, empty, and failed-load states are distinct, and a failed load never displays stale records as current data.
tickets.notes: USER.md · F-29. Designer 14 Aug 2026. Discuss before building. Do not copy office Edit from the user demo.

tickets.title: Address Book from profile menu
tickets.description: User profile menu includes Address Book (with Order History and Log out). Vue profile has RC Web Dev and Log out only.
acceptanceCriteria: Address Book appears in the regular-user profile menu.
Choosing Address Book opens the Address Book page.

tickets.title: My Address Book
tickets.description: Tab lists this user's personal locations (name + address) with Edit and Delete. Designer samples: Home Office, Temporary Location.
acceptanceCriteria: My Address Book lists only the current user's personal addresses, each with a location name and address.
Each personal row offers Edit and Delete. Colliers offices do not appear on this tab.

tickets.title: Office Addresses tab
tickets.description: Tab lists Colliers offices used on customize and shipping. User can view them. Designer also shows Edit on offices — do not copy that; office edits are admin (ADM-060).
acceptanceCriteria: Office Addresses lists the same Colliers offices used on customize and shipping, each with a distinct location name.
The user can view offices here. Adding, editing, or deleting company offices is not part of this user story.
tickets.notes: USER.md · F-29. Designer names every office 'Office Location' and offers Edit. Discuss; do not copy.

tickets.title: Search addresses
tickets.description: Search Addresses filters the active Address Book tab by location name or address text.
acceptanceCriteria: Typing in Search Addresses filters the visible list by location name or address text.
Clearing the search restores the full list for the active tab.

tickets.title: Add a personal address
tickets.description: + New Address opens a form. Save adds the location to My Address Book. Designer fields: nickname, name, email, phone, company, department, address 1/2, city, state, zip. Canada labels are USR-088.
acceptanceCriteria: New Address opens a form for a personal location.
Save adds the address to My Address Book and closes the form.
Final Save requires address nickname, recipient name, street, city, province, postal code, and country; invalid fields receive field-level guidance.
A successful save creates one personal-address record owned by the signed-in user; repeated clicks cannot create duplicates.

tickets.title: Edit a personal address
tickets.description: Edit fills the form with the saved personal address, including city / province / postal. Save updates that row.
acceptanceCriteria: Edit opens the form with the selected personal address already filled, including city, province, and postal code.
Save updates that row. Other addresses are unchanged.
Cancel or Back discards unsaved edits and leaves the stored address unchanged.
Users cannot edit another user’s personal address or change a company-office record through this form.

tickets.title: Delete a personal address
tickets.description: Delete removes a personal address from My Address Book. Users cannot delete Colliers offices from this page.
acceptanceCriteria: Delete removes the personal address from My Address Book after the user confirms.
Office addresses cannot be deleted from this page.
Canceling the confirmation leaves the address unchanged.
If the address is assigned to the active order, deletion is blocked or the user is required to replace it before continuing.

tickets.title: Canada address fields on Address Book
tickets.description: Designer form uses State and Zip. Colliers Canada should use Province and Postal, with Canada as the default country. Still to discuss.
acceptanceCriteria: The personal address form labels city, province, and postal code for Canadian addresses.
Country defaults to Canada. United States is not the default.
Province uses Canadian province/territory values and Postal Code accepts Canadian A1A 1A1 format case-insensitively, storing a normalized uppercase value.
Country defaults to Canada for a new address but does not overwrite the country of an existing record during edit.
tickets.notes: USER.md · F-29. Designer issue: State / Zip. Same Canada default discussion as ADM-N2, but this ticket is the user form.

tickets.title: Shipping can use personal Address Book entries
tickets.description: Select location on shipping includes the user's personal addresses as well as Colliers offices. Designer picker lists offices only; Repeat Order still fills NJ samples. Offices-not-NJ is USR-058. Still to discuss.
acceptanceCriteria: Select location on shipping includes this user's personal Address Book entries and Colliers offices.
A personal address saved in Address Book can be chosen as a ship-to location without retyping it.
tickets.notes: USER.md · F-29. Related USR-058 (offices, not NJ samples). Do not duplicate USR-058.

tickets.title: Order History
tickets.description: The user can see their own past business-card orders. Designer: profile → Order History (mock data, employee column, Back to Dashboard). Not admin Order History (ADM-030). Not in Vue. Still to discuss. Not in the V2 guide.
acceptanceCriteria: A signed-in user can open Order History and see only their own orders.
This page is not the admin Order History for all employees (ADM-030). Do not copy Back to Dashboard as a user dashboard.
tickets.notes: USER.md · F-30. Designer 14 Aug 2026. Discuss before building. Designer list is mock and did not gain a row after Place Order.

tickets.title: Order History from profile menu
tickets.description: User profile menu includes Order History. Vue profile has RC Web Dev and Log out only.
acceptanceCriteria: Order History appears in the regular-user profile menu.
Choosing Order History opens the same Order History page used from any other user shortcut.

tickets.title: Order History table
tickets.description: Table of this user's orders: order id, card / cardholder, box quantity, date, status, actions. Designer shows an Employee column and other people's names — that is admin-shaped. A user sees only their orders.
acceptanceCriteria: The table lists this user's orders with order id, card or cardholder, box quantity, date, status, and actions.
Orders placed by other people are not shown.
tickets.notes: USER.md · F-30. Quantity is boxes (same as cart), not a second printed-card column. Printed-card count is USR-046.

tickets.title: Search own orders
tickets.description: Search filters this user's Order History by cardholder name or order id. Designer label is Search by Name…
acceptanceCriteria: Search filters this user's orders by cardholder name or order id.
Clearing search restores the full list of this user's orders.

tickets.title: Filter own orders by status
tickets.description: Filter this user's orders by status. Designer options: All Statuses, Delivered, Shipped, Processing. Status set still to discuss.
acceptanceCriteria: The user can filter their orders by status, including an all-statuses option.
Changing the filter updates the table to matching orders only.
tickets.notes: USER.md · F-30. Discuss which statuses we keep.

tickets.title: View order card preview
tickets.description: View opens a preview of the business card on that order. Preview name, email, phone, and office must match the stored order. Designer issue: Alex Johnson with hubert.wolfeschlegelstein@… — do not copy.
acceptanceCriteria: View opens a preview of the business card for that order.
The preview name, email, phone, and office match the details stored on the order.
tickets.notes: USER.md · F-30. Same class of issue as ADM-N5, but this ticket is the user preview.

tickets.title: Repeat Order
tickets.description: Repeat Order recreates the cart and shipping draft from that order so the user can review and submit again. Designer Repeat Order still fills NJ sample streets. Offices-not-NJ is USR-058.
acceptanceCriteria: Repeat Order recreates the cart and shipping draft from that order so the user can review and submit again.
Ship-to locations on the repeated order are Colliers offices or this user's saved addresses, not New Jersey sample addresses.
tickets.notes: USER.md · F-30. Related USR-058 and USR-089. Do not copy ADM-N4 as a second ticket.

tickets.title: Confirmed orders appear in history
tickets.description: After a successful confirmation, the order appears in this user's Order History. Designer list is mock; Place Order did not add a row.
acceptanceCriteria: After a successful confirmation, the new order appears in this user's Order History.
The history row shows the same product, box quantity, and addresses that were confirmed.
tickets.notes: USER.md · F-30. Confirmation still clears the cart (USR-062) and does not collect payment (USR-053).

tickets.title: Admin scoped from designer
tickets.description: Walked the designer admin preview (admin / 123). Wrote ADMIN.md and the ADM-010…ADM-083 stories. No admin screens in Vue yet. Do not copy designer issues ADM-N1–ADM-N5.
acceptanceCriteria: The approved admin scope is represented by the ADM-010 through ADM-083 ticket groups.
Known designer issues are captured separately and are not treated as approved behavior.

tickets.title: Admin login and nav
tickets.description: Not in Vue. Designer: login admin / 123. Header ADMIN, Catalogue, Manage Addresses, Manage Titles. Profile: Admin Panel, Address Book, Order History, Log out.
acceptanceCriteria: Valid admin credentials open the admin application shell.
The admin shell provides the approved navigation and profile actions on every admin page.

tickets.title: Admin login admin / 123
tickets.description: Login screen accepts admin / 123 and opens the admin shell.
acceptanceCriteria: Entering admin / 123 grants access to the admin shell.
Invalid credentials keep the user on the login screen and display a clear error without exposing admin content.

tickets.title: Admin header nav
tickets.description: Header shows ADMIN, Catalogue, Manage Addresses, Manage Titles. Not in Vue; user header is catalogue only.
acceptanceCriteria: The admin header shows ADMIN, Catalogue, Manage Addresses, and Manage Titles.
Each navigation item opens the correct route and indicates the active page.

tickets.title: Admin profile menu
tickets.description: Profile: Admin Panel, Address Book, Order History, Log out. Vue profile has RC Web Dev and Log out only. Address Book page work is ADM-080.
acceptanceCriteria: The profile menu shows Admin Panel, Address Book, Order History, and Log out.
Each option performs the expected navigation or ends the admin session.
tickets.notes: ADMIN.md · F-12. Address Book: ADM-080. Order History: ADM-036.

tickets.title: Admin Dashboard
tickets.description: Not in Vue. System Options only. No Total Orders / Pending Approvals / Active Users tiles (TC-26 is outdated).
acceptanceCriteria: The dashboard displays the approved System Options tiles.
Each tile opens its corresponding admin screen and displays current supporting counts where required.

tickets.title: System Options tiles
tickets.description: Order History, Invoice History, Reporting, Manage Addresses, Manage Titles.

tickets.title: Live address count

tickets.title: Live title count

tickets.title: Order History

Search, status filtering, viewing, and repeat-order actions work on the displayed records.

tickets.title: Order History table

tickets.title: Search orders by name

acceptanceCriteria: Entering an employee name filters the table to matching orders.
Clearing the search restores the full order list and no-match searches show a clear empty state.

tickets.title: Filter orders by status
tickets.description: Filter: All / Delivered / Shipped / Processing.
acceptanceCriteria: All, Delivered, Shipped, and Processing filters return only the expected orders.
Changing or clearing the filter updates results without altering the underlying order data.

tickets.title: View order card preview

acceptanceCriteria: View opens a preview for the selected order row.

tickets.title: Repeat Order

acceptanceCriteria: Repeat Order adds the selected historical card and quantity to the current cart.

tickets.title: Order History from profile menu

acceptanceCriteria: Order History in the profile menu opens the same Order History screen used elsewhere.

tickets.title: Invoice History

acceptanceCriteria: The Invoice History screen displays the available invoice records.

tickets.title: Invoice table

acceptanceCriteria: Each invoice row shows Invoice ID, Date, Department, Amount, and Status.
Status is limited to the approved Paid, Pending, or Overdue values.

tickets.title: Download invoice
tickets.description: Download action on an invoice row.
acceptanceCriteria: Selecting Download retrieves the invoice associated with that row.
The downloaded file opens successfully and contains the matching invoice identifier and amount.

tickets.title: Reporting

tickets.title: Monthly Spend Overview
tickets.description: Reporting: monthly spend overview.

The values and period labels match the reporting data source.

tickets.title: Recent Activity

acceptanceCriteria: Recent Activity lists the latest relevant order or administrative events.
Each entry shows enough information to identify the event and when it occurred.

tickets.title: Spend by Department

acceptanceCriteria: Spend by Department shows each department and its corresponding total.
Department totals reconcile with the overall spend for the selected period.

tickets.title: Export Data

acceptanceCriteria: The user can generate a report using the available report controls.

tickets.title: Manage Addresses
tickets.description: Own screen. Not in Vue. List, add, edit, remove. Do not rebuild Edit Supplier Details.
acceptanceCriteria: Manage Addresses lists existing offices and provides add, edit, and remove actions.
Changes made through the screen are reflected wherever managed office addresses are used.

tickets.title: List office addresses
tickets.description: List of office addresses on Manage Addresses.
acceptanceCriteria: Each active office appears once with enough address information to distinguish it.
The list reflects additions, edits, and removals without requiring stale sample data.

tickets.title: Add address
tickets.description: Add opens the New Address form (ADM-065).
acceptanceCriteria: Add Address opens a blank New Address form.
Saving valid required fields adds one new office to the address list.
Final Save requires Address Name, Street, City, Province, Postal Code, and Country; invalid fields block save and retain the entered values.
A successful save creates exactly one managed office record and makes it available to customization and shipping after refresh or reload.

tickets.title: Remove address
tickets.description: Remove an office from the list.
acceptanceCriteria: Remove targets the selected office and requires confirmation before deletion.
After confirmation, the office disappears from the managed list and is no longer selectable for new orders.
Deletion requires confirmation and cannot be triggered by clicking elsewhere in the row.
An office referenced by an active draft or historical order is deactivated or blocked from deletion according to the approved data rule; historical order data is not corrupted.

tickets.title: Edit address
tickets.description: Edit opens Update Existing Address (ADM-065). Designer issue: fields do not fill (ADM-N1).
acceptanceCriteria: Edit opens the selected address with every existing field prefilled correctly.
Saving changes updates that record without creating a duplicate address.
Cancel restores the persisted values and produces no update request.
A successful edit updates the same record ID and does not create a duplicate office.

tickets.title: New / edit address form
tickets.description: Required: Address Name, Street, City, State/Province, ZIP/Postal, Country. Designer issues: default US (ADM-N2), empty Save Draft (ADM-N3).
acceptanceCriteria: The form includes Address Name, Street, City, Province, Postal Code, and Country as required fields.
Invalid or missing required values prevent final submission and display field-level guidance.

tickets.title: Address form actions
tickets.description: Save Draft, Add New Address / Update Address, Back to Addresses.
acceptanceCriteria: Back to Addresses returns without unintentionally saving changes.
Add/Update saves valid data, while Save Draft preserves an incomplete record only when draft behavior is supported.

tickets.title: Customize and shipping use admin addresses
tickets.description: After this list exists, customize offices and shipping savedAddresses should use it. Vue customize is already Colliers; shipping still has NJ samples.
acceptanceCriteria: Customize and shipping load office choices from the managed address list.
An admin address change appears in both workflows and New Jersey seed addresses never appear.

tickets.title: Manage Titles
tickets.description: Own screen. Not in Vue. List designations (PMP, LEED AP, …). Add, delete, inline edit.
acceptanceCriteria: Manage Titles lists existing designations and provides add, edit, and delete actions.
Saved title changes are reflected in the customization designation control.
tickets.notes: ADMIN.md · F-15 · BUSINESS-RULES.md calls this Manage Designations

tickets.title: List designations
tickets.description: List of titles / designations.
acceptanceCriteria: Each active designation appears once in the list.
The list updates immediately after a successful add, edit, or delete action.

tickets.title: Add title
tickets.description: Add a designation to the list.
acceptanceCriteria: A non-empty unique designation can be added successfully.
Blank or duplicate values are rejected with a clear message.
Uniqueness is checked after trimming whitespace and without regard to letter case.
A successful add creates exactly one active designation and makes it available to customization without duplicating existing values.

tickets.title: Delete title
tickets.description: Remove a designation.
acceptanceCriteria: Deleting a designation requires confirmation and removes the selected value.
Deleting one designation does not remove or modify any other designation.
A designation already used by a saved cart or historical order is deactivated or blocked according to the approved data rule; existing records keep their original display value.
Canceling the confirmation leaves the designation active and unchanged.

tickets.title: Inline edit title
tickets.description: Pencil → inline field → save (check) or cancel (X).
acceptanceCriteria: The pencil action changes only the selected row into an editable field.
Save commits the edited value and Cancel restores the original value without changes.
Blank, whitespace-only, and case-insensitive duplicate values cannot be saved.
Only one row can be in edit mode at a time, and a failed save keeps that row editable with a clear error.

tickets.title: Customize titles come from Manage Titles
tickets.description: Customize job-title dropdown is hardcoded in products.js. After ADM-070, use this list.
acceptanceCriteria: The customization designation control loads active values from Manage Titles.
Added, edited, or deleted titles are reflected without changing existing saved cart items.

acceptanceCriteria: The project includes a repeatable automated test command with documented setup.

tickets.title: Establish the Vue 2 application baseline
tickets.description: Replace the Vue 3 runtime and build assumptions with a clean Vue 2-compatible baseline that runs as a standalone browser application and can later be moved into Clay Studio.
acceptanceCriteria: The project installs from a clean checkout and starts with the documented development command.
The production build completes successfully and opens without a blank screen, console error, or unhandled rejection.
package.json and the lockfile resolve Vue 2.x and Vue 2-compatible versions of the router, state, test, and UI dependencies.
No Vue 3-only bootstrap or component syntax remains, including createApp, script setup, Teleport, or Vue 3-only lifecycle APIs.
The README records the supported Node version, install command, development command, test command, and production-build command.
tickets.notes: Foundation for all Vue 2 implementation tickets.

tickets.title: Define Vue 2 routes and hash-navigation fallback
tickets.description: Create the page architecture in Vue 2 and ensure navigation can operate with Vue Router in the standalone build and a hash fallback when BF.router is unavailable.
acceptanceCriteria: Every approved V2 page has one documented route and one owning page component; modal or drawer UI is not represented as a separate page route unless it must be directly addressable.
Direct loading and browser refresh work for catalogue, details, customization, cart/shipping, review, confirmation-safe-state, address book, login, and approved admin routes.
Navigation falls back to window.location.hash when BF.router is undefined and never throws a BF.router undefined error.
Unknown routes lead to a safe not-found or catalogue page and do not leave a blank application shell.
Back and forward navigation do not clear the active order draft unless the user has successfully submitted or explicitly cleared it.
tickets.notes: Use hash routes compatible with the future Clay Studio host.

tickets.title: Create Vue 2 reactive order and shipping state
tickets.description: Create a single order-state model for cart lines, shipping groups, locations, allocations, totals, language, and submission state using Vue 2-safe reactivity.
acceptanceCriteria: The model has one source of truth for ordered box quantity; printed-card count, price, badge count, and allocation totals are derived values.
Adding or deleting reactive keys uses Vue.set, Vue.delete, or an equivalent Vue 2-safe replacement pattern.
Creating, moving, allocating, removing, and clearing items cannot produce negative values, duplicate IDs, orphan allocations, or mismatched order totals.
All new cards enter Shipping Group 1; a new split group begins empty; moving a card preserves total ordered quantity.
State-transition helpers have automated tests independent of rendered components.
tickets.notes: Implements the V2 cart and split-order invariants.

tickets.title: Create adapters and named-action helpers for FileMaker
tickets.description: Separate browser-test data from future FileMaker operations. Define helper files and named-action contracts for products, addresses, designations, order submission, and order lookup where approved.
acceptanceCriteria: The standalone application uses mock adapters with the same request and response shapes as the future FileMaker adapters.
Each external operation has one named action or adapter function with documented input, success output, validation failure, request failure, and timeout behavior.
Page components do not call FileMaker, BF, fetch, or mock data directly; they call the adapter interface.
Requests expose loading state, prevent duplicate submission where applicable, and surface a recoverable error without clearing valid user state.
No credential, server URL, FileMaker file name, or production record identifier is hardcoded in a component.
tickets.notes: Mike can implement FileMaker scripts against these contracts while Carlos builds the Vue 2 front end.

tickets.title: Port shared UI components to Vue 2
tickets.description: Port the reusable shell and controls before page-by-page development: header, footer, buttons, form fields, selects, multi-select, card preview, drawers, dialogs, loading, empty, and error states.
acceptanceCriteria: Every shared component compiles in Vue 2 and uses supported props, events, slots, and v-model conventions.
Inputs expose label, required state, help text, invalid state, and error text without relying on placeholder text as the only label.
Dialog and drawer components close through their explicit controls and Escape, restore focus, and do not allow background interaction while open.
Components remain usable at approved desktop and mobile widths without clipped content or nested scrolling that traps the user.
Shared components contain no Colliers order rules that belong in state helpers or page orchestration.
tickets.notes: Complete before porting feature pages to reduce repeated migration work.

tickets.title: Add Vue 2 quality and migration gates
tickets.description: Create automated and manual checks that prevent Vue 3 code, broken business rules, or Clay-incompatible coupling from entering the Vue 2 delivery.
acceptanceCriteria: CI or the documented local verification command runs linting, unit tests, and a production build and returns a non-zero exit code on failure.
A dependency check confirms Vue 2.x and rejects known Vue 3-only packages or APIs.

The critical business-rule suite covers 50-character name, 40-character email, cart merging, quantity math, empty split groups, product moves, allocation reconciliation, review, failed submit, successful submit, and cart reset.
The standalone build can complete the approved order flow using mock adapters with network delay and forced-error modes.
A migration checklist confirms that components do not directly depend on browser-only storage, Vue Router, or FileMaker globals without an adapter or fallback.
tickets.notes: Release gate for standalone Vue 2 and later Clay Studio migration.

projectContext.deliveryTarget: Standalone Vue 2 web application prepared for later Clay Studio / FM BetterForms migration
projectContext.sourceOfTruth: Colliers Business Card Portal — Business Rules & Testing Guide, V2 Reference

releaseConstraints: Use Vue 2-compatible syntax, lifecycle hooks, libraries, and build tooling. Do not use Vue 3-only APIs such as createApp, Composition API-only patterns, script setup, Teleport, or Vue 3-only packages.
Keep business logic out of page templates. Put reusable calculations, normalization, validation, cart comparison, shipping allocation, and data-access logic in helper or service modules.
The standalone web build must run without FileMaker so the team can test it in a browser. FileMaker and Clay Studio integration must remain behind replaceable adapters or named actions.
Use camelCase model keys and Vue.set or Vue.delete when adding or removing reactive object properties at runtime.
Do not assume Vue Router is available in Clay Studio. Navigation must have a hash-based fallback and must survive a browser refresh on supported routes.
Do not include credit-card payment, calculated shipping charges, SKU display, dark mode, invoice history, reporting, or a footer language selector in the V2 release.
Use approved Colliers addresses and designations. Prototype New Jersey addresses and mismatched sample identity data must not appear in user-facing flows.
definitionOfDone: Every acceptance criterion for the ticket passes in the standalone Vue 2 build.
The feature works at supported desktop and mobile widths without clipped, overlapping, or unreachable controls.
Loading, empty, invalid-input, and failed-request states are handled where the feature can encounter them; the application does not silently fail.
No browser-console error or unhandled promise rejection is produced by the completed flow.
All user-facing English and French strings use the application translation layer; product data and user-entered values are not translated.

Business state remains correct after navigation and repeated actions; one click or submission must not create duplicate cart items, groups, addresses, or orders unless the rule explicitly requires it.
Automated tests cover calculation, comparison, validation, or state-transition logic introduced by the ticket; the relevant manual business-rule test is also recorded.
The ticket notes identify dependencies, unresolved product decisions, and any intentional difference from the V2 business-rules guide.

inScope: Standalone Vue 2 application baseline and reusable page/component architecture
English, Bilingual, and French business-card products at $63.00 per box of 250 cards
Customization, live preview, cart, shipping groups, split order, review, submission, and confirmation
English/French interface controlled from the header
Approved address and designation management required by the ordering flow
requiresProductDecisionBeforeBuild: Personal Address Book details beyond the agreed saved-address shipping requirement
Order History and Repeat Order behavior
Whether incomplete address drafts are supported
Deletion behavior for addresses or designations referenced by historical records
